rfm_tuples.R: Same venue sales decreased Topgolf segment revenues by $123.3 million in the 2024 fiscal year and increased Topgolf segment revenues by $9.2 million and $117.8 million for fiscal years 2023 and 2022, respectively... our ability to drive same venue sales, which have recently declined, and there are material risks to our ability to increase such sales.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Verify candor of same-venue trajectory disclosure. Check that magnitude (-$123.3M) and directional admission ('recently declined') are stated without euphemism, in plain dollar terms, in the risk factor (not buried in MD&A).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Disclosure is direct and quantitative; multi-year comparable series ($117.8M -> $9.2M -> -$123.3M) shows the full deceleration arc; risk factor headline explicitly says 'recently declined' and 'material risks'. Same-venue % of segment (72.4% / 72.1% / 73.5%) also given.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Honest. Topgolf same-venue is the company's most-watched KPI; management volunteered the magnitude of the deterioration and labeled the forward risk as 'material.' This is the opposite of cosmetic disclosure.

rfm_tuples.R: During the fourth quarter of 2024 we... recorded a goodwill impairment charge of $1,352.4 million and a trade name impairment charge of $99.6 million to write-down the Topgolf trade name to its new estimated fair value... impairment losses of $1,452.0 million on goodwill and intangible assets associated with our Topgolf operating segment.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE A: Check that the impairment magnitude, segment, drivers, and methodology are disclosed and tied to operating reality (declining same-venue sales, slowed venue openings).
rfm_tuples.M_value: $1.45B Topgolf impairment booked in Q4 2024; drivers explicitly named: 'sustained unfavorable macroeconomic conditions, elevated inflation and interest rates... downward pressure on consumer and corporate discretionary spending... declines in same venue sales... decrease the number of planned venue openings.' Combined income/market approach disclosed.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: This is the textbook honest-bad-news pattern. Management took a massive write-down BEFORE the spin and explicitly tied causation to the deteriorating KPI in C1. Honesty-alpha framework should NOT short this — they cleared the deck.

rfm_tuples.R: We expect to execute the separation [spin-off of Topgolf] in the second half of 2025. The transaction will be subject to general market conditions and other customary conditions, including receipt of regulatory approvals, an opinion from tax counsel and/or a private letter ruling from the Internal Revenue Service... execution of intercompany agreements, further due diligence as appropriate and final approval by our Board. There can be no assurance regarding the form and timing of the separation or its completion.
rfm_tuples.f: MODE B: Check whether spin language is hyped/inevitable vs hedged. Strong-form distress shops drop 'separation will create value' boilerplate without the conditionality. Look for explicit no-assurance disclaimer.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Conditionality is dense and specific: PLR/tax opinion, regulatory approvals, intercompany agreements, further due diligence, board approval, AND a final 'no assurance regarding form, timing, or completion.' Stated rationale (strategic focus, capital allocation, simplified structure, distinct theses) is generic but not deceptive.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Adequately hedged. The conditions list reads like real M&A legal disclosure, not a promotional press release. Slight UNV on whether the spin actually executes, but the company is not lying about uncertainty.

rfm_tuples.R: [2023 Term Loan B] bears interest at variable rates. As a result, increases in interest rates increase the cost of servicing our indebtedness and could materially reduce our profitability and cash flows... Restrictive covenants explicitly enumerated. No covenant breach or waiver disclosed. ABL fixed-charge coverage requirement noted.

rfm_tuples.R: We continue to focus on our market share leadership position in both golf clubs and golf balls by continuously investing in research and development... summary: CALY's FY24 10-K is a textbook honest-bad-news filing. Management took a $1.45B Topgolf impairment, disclosed the same-venue sales decline in dollar terms ($-123.3M YoY) with multi-year arc, named Acushnet as dominant ball-market competitor, listed all major risks specifically (not generically), and hedged the H2 2025 spin with dense conditionality. Auditor (Deloitte) continues, ICFR is effective, no covenant amendments, $50M voluntary Term Loan B paydown demonstrates real liquidity. The R/f/M framework should mark this as PASS-heavy (8 PASS, 1 MOD on China supply concentration, 0 SEV/RED). The framework would NOT short this name — which is the correct call given the +132% forward return. Key Mode-B finding: the absence of CEO transition, 10b5-1 sales, or covenant amendments clustered to the spin announcement is itself the honesty signal. This is the kind of name the honesty-alpha framework should specifically EXCLUDE from shorts, validating the exclusion-as-alpha thesis.
